title: Existence of a section of O(1) giving an injective multiplication F(-1) -> F with cokernel pushed forward from the associated hyperplane
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on cohomology of projective space
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for any coherent module F on projective n-space over an infinite field, a nonzero section s of O(1) such that multiplication F(-1) -> F is injective with cokernel of the form i_*G for the associated hyperplane i : H -> P^n. The proof first computes the map on D_+(T_0) as multiplication by a_0 + sum a_i x_i on the finite module M, then shows injectivity by choosing that element outside all associated primes of M, which is possible because Ass(M) is finite and each prime cuts out a proper k-subvector space, so a finite union of proper subspaces cannot exhaust the infinite field (proof lines 6513-6543). The final step identifies the cokernel as annihilated by the ideal sheaf of H and descends it to the hyperplane (proof lines 6544-6549). H3: the associated-primes-to-subspaces reduction and the geometric descent of the cokernel are independent research-level moves over an infinite field.
